hook: Telangana's October GST hit *₹4,593 crore*, up 17%
hook_b: Petrol and liquor VAT jumped 31%. What does that say?
tldr: Telangana's GST rose 17% and VAT 31% in October; ₹1,402 crore more than last October.

beats.what: Telangana collected ₹4,593 crore GST in October, up from ₹3,914 crore a year ago.
beats.why: Sakshi credits Hyderabad's IT, services, pharma and auto-parts activity.
beats.care: More state revenue means more room for schemes. VAT growth reflects fuel and liquor sales.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Per Sakshi, citing Centre's GST data: Telangana's October GST rose from ₹3,914 crore to ₹4,593 crore (+₹679 crore, 17%). VAT on petroleum and liquor rose from ₹2,342 crore to ₹3,065 crore (+₹723 crore, 31%). Together, ₹1,402 crore more than last October. For April–October, GST plus VAT reached ₹51,563 crore vs ₹44,023 crore last year, about ₹7,500 crore more. Sakshi attributes growth to IT/ITES and corporate services in Hyderabad, plus manufacturing, pharma and auto parts.

cards.q: Extra ₹1,400 crore: where should it go first?

viz.l: GST + VAT, Apr–Oct (₹44,023 cr last year)

insight: VAT on petrol and liquor grew faster than GST: 31% vs 17%, per Sakshi's figures.

learn.t: VAT = value added tax; states still levy it on petrol, diesel and liquor, which sit outside GST.

watch: November collections, and whether cyclone rain dents economic activity.
